entries.defect: The run starts in Cairo and the only drum village is bambara-village, so the player must cross the continent before any step of the chain exists.
The run starts with no shovel; the player must buy one before the upstream dig, or the boulder only answers digNoShovel and no artefact is received.
Nothing points the player to Bambara Village as the one village with a message; every other chief only nods, so the right village is found by chance.
The chiefStepsOut toast fires in every village on village kind alone and promises a drum message that outside Bambara never comes.
The chiefWalk journal entry is written in every village on first step-out and tells the player to follow the chief while the actual act is to stand before him and the drummer.
The player must hear distinguishable syllables over drums and ambience at shipped defaults on both backends; the generated speech plan alone proves no audible output.
The mixed speech-plus-drum peak (about 1.34) exceeds headroom without a limiter, so clipping can damage the tonal distinctions the player needs.
Village speech is not held while the drums beat, so children's CALL words and adult words can land on the 16 strikes and both get squeezed.
A word is recorded as heard by distance alone: with no audio context, a zero speech slider, a muted tab or a silent plan the utterance still fires, so the note and journal appear with no sound.
observePhrase records every atom immediately without tracking completed playback, so interrupted or partly heard speech appears fully learned.
The drum message's peak is scaled by the ambience volume, so a lowered ambience slider silences the chief's message while it is still recorded as heard and shown on paper.

The player must recognise the four-syllable high/low pattern and associate the same pattern across spoken voice, written syllables and low/high drum strikes; noticing that somebody spoke or drummed teaches nothing.

The player must stand within TALK reach (10 m) of an adult or weaver or CALL reach (34 m) of a child to get the word, the note and the E invitation; beyond that the figure neither speaks nor gestures.

Hearing and speaker targeting do not derive their reach from the speaker's talk/call reach: speechChannel falls back to the legacy hearingRadius 10 and speechTarget takes a caller-supplied maximum, so the highlighted speaker may be unusable at the bank's distances.

The speech-floor deadline force-speaks a word held past its hold even when another exchange owns the floor or the speaker is blocked, giving overlapping speech or a word whose visible consequence has already passed, reported only as a dev defect.
holdsFloor ignores the separate consequence reservation, so a wordless cry can be permitted during a consequence that still blocks other words.
Both adult words yield while any child can hear and DIG needs a second free adult clear of the children's grounds, so RIVER/DIG can be deferred up to 240 s and the waiting player sees idle adults.
The player must catch the moment a child calls RIVER and points at the water and follow the children's departure to the bank, or is left searching an empty teaching area.
Named cause 1 (two rocks at the ends of a bank stretch) is addressed in code and layout but bank placement and upstream consistency are only certified by the picture on both backends.

The two bank rocks are drawn identically and only the river's streak shader distinguishes upstream from downstream, so the direction ambiguity stays wherever the water is off-screen or its flow is faint.
The direction announcement points at the far rock, so UPSTREAM/DOWNSTREAM can be read as 'over there / to the other rock', a reading only the loom can prune.
The loom teaches UPSTREAM/DOWNSTREAM a second time only with a river and a helper and can give way to a shipped plan, so without both the direction words keep only the ambiguous bank reading.

Named cause 3 is still open: bank utterances carry one concept each but nothing consults heard or understood meanings, so a direction word and the tap's ROCK arrive one hearing gap apart as two unknowns.
The player must see ROCK applied both to a stationary touch and an ordinary climbed boulder; arrivals alone permit wrong readings such as 'safe', 'goal' or 'made it'.
When the catcher's walk to his stone is blocked the tap and its ROCK are skipped and the run opens anyway, so run counters advance while a whole round teaches ROCK only as 'arrived'.
Becoming safe at a rock is separate from hand contact, so a missing contact stand or expired approach leaves a successful runner without an audible ROCK result.

Without an ordinary climbable boulder the bank stage either cannot be built or its boulder lesson stays silent, so ROCK never transfers beyond the game's targets, which the upstream boulder depends on.
The off-game boulder lesson can be abandoned after failed approaches or its overtime bound while the game continues, removing the strongest evidence against reading ROCK as 'base'.
Gather and regroup have timeout exits, so a direction can be announced before everybody reached their stations, over a spatially incoherent starting arrangement.
A run timeout accepts runners that never reached the far rock and permits the side swap, so repeated timeouts make the announced directions describe intended rather than seen movement.
Named cause 2 requires recognisable adult results: the full jar set down at the stand and the finished pit, post or planted patch must be shown in frame in the play-through.

The fixed-loop observation still holds: the adult catalogue is four situations on a fixed interval grid and the bank game alternates direction at fixed utterance moments, so the errands read as a repeating loop.
adultErrands.dwellSeconds is still in balance and the debug menu but no code reads it, a dead knob that misleads a tester.
The note stands 2.6 s; the player must be within reach and get the speaker highlighted in that window so the target holds the note long enough to press E and open the guess dialog.
Label lifetime adds only inter-atom pauses, not the additional atoms' speaking time, so a long phrase can outlast its label.
dropFloorLabels removes the TARGETED note and clears its invitation when any other floor word falls, so a player walking up to press E loses the invitation mid-approach.

The player must read the label above the actual speaking figure, including small children and a child lifted onto a boulder; the height helper alone does not prove correct projection or unobstructed rendering.
The player must discover the actual guess key; speechTarget still carries older SPACE wording beside newer E wording, and bindings and localized invitations were not verified.
Any open dialog removes the label invitation and the guess dialog hides its source label, so the dialog must itself preserve the selected syllables before those cues disappear.
A label needs only one previously heard atom, not the whole phrase, so a mixed known/unheard phrase exposes readings whose memory entries cannot yet be edited.
Guess drafts are keyed by utterance, so a phrase with a repeated atom binds two inputs to one draft and the last one typed wins silently.
The player must enter, revise and clear a hypothesis for the exact heard utterance; notes are unchecked free text, so usable correction rather than an assumed correctness signal is required.
Repeat observations keep only the first hearing's day and place with no action or phrase context, so a journal entry cannot recover which gesture or result supported a later guess.
Every chronicle entry opens the journal unless do-not-disturb is on, so the book opens over the scene in the same frame as the drum dialog and can hide or clutter the paper.
The drum paper opens by itself only if no other dialog is open at the last beat, so a player in the guess dialog gets no paper and must find the journal reopen button.
CHIEF is taught only by pressing use at the drummer while the chief is in his hut; once he is out the same key sends the message, so the order of play decides whether CHIEF is ever heard.
The lexicon holds six concepts including CHIEF while the material still speaks of five words, so teaching and glossary coverage must include the sixth.

To get the errand the player must press use at the hut, wait for the chief's walk to the drummer, then request the message there within chiefStaySeconds and hear all 16 strikes; the first arrival does not deliver it by itself.
Using the hut while the chief is outside and calling while he walks outward both do nothing, so visible feedback must explain these silent presses.
Recalling a chief walking home must deliver the automatic message when he returns to the drummer; losing that arrival event turns an accepted recall into silence.
Requesting repeats while the chief stands beside the drummer refreshes his stay, but the interaction layer must actually dispatch the replay rather than only keep him standing.
The chief walks a straight interpolated path without collision resolution and can pass through scenery, as at the maasai-village rock.
Walk and stay use wall-clock timestamps and consume one boundary per tick, so after a long interruption successive ticks can exhaust his stay at once.
A resumed snapshot clears chiefOutside and the walk, so a player who loads beside a chief in the open finds him in his hut and a give tried at once gets findNeedsChief.
Message selection depends only on whether rockArtefact was given, but no interaction code proves the legacy cultural-gift or trust gates are gone.

A sounding drum plan keeps its original message while the give changes currentDrumMessage, so display and animation must follow the retained plan or the player reads the answer while hearing the errand.
receiveDrumMessage records all four atoms as heard with the drum village as first place even if no villager taught them, so the glossary shows unheard words as heard.
Displaying a drum-message atom does not itself record it as heard, so if the playback caller fails to observe it setHypothesis silently rejects the player's reading.
The drumMessage journal claims 'I have heard every one of them in the lanes and at the water' regardless of truth, so a player who goes straight to the chief reads a false claim.
The player must interpret the errand as RIVER · UPSTREAM · ROCK · DIG and distinguish its travel-world destination from the children's two local play rocks.
UPSTREAM is the rising pattern and DOWNSTREAM its reverse by construction, so the claim that all vocabulary assignments roll per run is inaccurate.
Other concepts, including nonadjacent errand words, can also form a reversal pair, so a player generalising 'reversed tones mean opposites' can draw a false conclusion.
Memory serialization stores notes but no vocabulary mapping, so a restore must reattach the matching run vocabulary or restored notes silently acquire different meanings.
The player must find and edit the glossary and reread deciphered messages in both English and German; the glossary components and language files were not verified.

Deciphering must work in either order: the paper and journal share one memory, so earlier messages must be retained, reopenable from the journal and re-rendered once the direction words are understood.

In the bird's-eye view the player must read upstream from the scrolling streaks and follow the Niger 1.6–2.4° (about 3 days, farther when candidates were rejected) to the seeded block; searching beside the village cannot succeed.

Only the block's upright size and cleared dressing set it apart and nothing links it on screen to the village's play rocks, so its conspicuousness in real travel views and the ROCK transfer are unproven.
Placement accepts dry, unblocked probes on either bank without proving a traversable route, so geometric validity does not guarantee the player can reach the excavation.
An exhausted placement search returns the village coordinate with upstreamDeg zero and no unvouched flag when that footprint is dry, so the destination no longer satisfies the chief's upstream clue.
The player must press dig in travel mode within digRadius 3 units (0.3°) of the block centre; the find then enters the bar as 'Find from the Boulder' outside pack capacity.
Excavation range is measured to the boulder's centre while its footprint blocks movement, so collision and dig reach must leave a reachable standing position that passes the test.
Socket and boulder distances are plain lat/lon hypots without cos(lat), so the accepted reach is an ellipse rather than the drawn circle and standing at the drawn spot can fail the check.
The dig at the boulder succeeds without the errand ever being heard, so the player can shortcut the language chain and the chain cannot prove the words were used.
The rockArtefact and mouldFitted journal entries hand the player translations ('against its own pull', 'the way it wants to go'), against the spec rule that nothing translates.

The give happens only by activating the carried find in the inventory bar within giveReach 2.6 m of the chief standing in the open; merely returning to the village or any other spot yields findNeedsChief and the errand keeps sounding.
findTooltip says 'Click it before the chief' but the pointer is locked in the place scene, so the click cannot work and the working digit key is never named.
After the give the answer RIVER · DOWNSTREAM is beaten at once or on the chief's arrival, and the player must wait for its last beat before it is recorded and shown.
The clay form enters the bar in the same store write as the give with no drawn hand-over, so only a new bar slot and a journal line show it happened.

The player must receive RIVER · DOWNSTREAM together with a readable mould that carries the destination and next action (DIG is deliberately absent), and use it to recognise the downstream target; missing the wordless object removes essential information.

RIVER · DOWNSTREAM underdetermines the socket: it names no starting point, and the Bandiagara socket lies about 0.8° east of the Niger, so nothing tells the player where to begin or to leave the river.
The player must stand within 0.3° of the talus-foot landmark origin in travel mode and activate the clay form; inside a settlement it only answers formInSettlement.

Fitting the form only raises the transient pocSolved placeholder toast and a journal page; victory is never set, so the chain has no unmistakable end state and a player looking elsewhere can miss its completion.
